bug_semantics: withMobileAuth in src/middleware.ts (matcher /api/mobile/:path*) treats mere presence of an Auth-Key request header as authorization and returns NextResponse.next() without comparing the value to any server-side secret and without overwriting request headers. JWT verification is skipped. Downstream handlers, including src/app/api/mobile/search/route.ts, then JSON.parse a client-supplied g header as the authenticated user and query purchased course/video titles and IDs. An unauthenticated caller can send Auth-Key: anything plus a forged g JSON body and receive HTTP 200 search results (CWE-306/CWE-200). CVE.org CVE-2026-52021 is PUBLISHED (MITRE CNA; GHSA withdrawn_at null).

potential_fix.approach: In withMobileAuth, reject the Auth-Key path unless the header equals a non-empty server-side secret (the same equality pattern /api/mobile/signin already uses against EXTERNAL_LOGIN_AUTH_SECRET; do not treat header presence as auth). On that path, copy headers and delete('g') before NextResponse.next(). On the JWT path, keep overwriting g from the verified payload only. In search/courses handlers, do not JSON.parse a client g value as identity unless middleware set it after successful auth.
potential_fix.rationale: The disclosure sink is NextResponse.next() on any Auth-Key, which skips JWT and forwards attacker headers so search JSON.parse(g) as the user. Requiring a secret match closes the unauthenticated gate; stripping or overwriting g closes identity forgery even when a legitimate service key is presented.
